rot.edge.ideia.ex1.e1: Now there are more pawns on the board. You play Black, and the board flips.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.e2: Look at the pawns: none can advance, because each has another pawn in front of it. They are blocked.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.e3: With the pawns stuck, only the kings move. And White cannot pass the turn with a pawn move.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.e4: The white king's target is the pawn on c5. If your king moves away from it, the white king captures it.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.e5: To defend it, your king must stay near b6 and answer every white move by keeping the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.livre.fala: Keep playing as Black and see how White attacks.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.p: Black to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.certo: Exactly! On a7, your king stands on the same rank as the white king, with three squares between them.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to take the king to a7, on the same rank as the white king, with three squares between them.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6a6.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6a6.2: The white king goes to e6, on the same rank. There are three squares between the kings and Black is to move: White has the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6c7.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6c7.2: The white king goes to e6. If the black king returns to b6, the white king reaches d6 and keeps the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6a5.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6a5.2: The white king goes to d7. If the black king returns to b6, the white king reaches d6 and keeps the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6b7.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6b7.2: The white king goes to d7, on the same rank. Only c7 lies between the kings and Black is to move: White has the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.1: Three squares between the kings, and White is to move: an odd number, so you have the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.2: The white king approaches along the seventh rank, towards the black pawns.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.3: You answer on b7. Only c7 lies between the kings: you still have the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.4: The white king steps down to d6 and attacks the pawn on c5.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.5: You defend with the king on b6. The pawn on c6 stands between the kings, and it counts as a square: just one, an odd number.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.6: You have the opposition. The white king cannot capture either pawn, because your king defends both.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.7: And White cannot pass the turn with a pawn move. The white king has to step back.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.8: If the white king tries another square, the answer is the same: your king goes to the same rank and leaves an odd number.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.9: That is why a7 is the right square: from there, your king always returns to b6 with the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.10: Now let's see the attack: how White gets the opposition when it seems to belong to Black.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.e1: Now you play White. This position comes from a study by Brandon2021 on Lichess.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.e2: The pawns are still blocked. Your king wants to reach the black pawns on c5 and c6 to capture them.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.e3: The kings are on the same rank, with three squares between them, and White is to move. Black has the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.e4: If your king comes closer, the black king follows on the same rank and keeps the number odd.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.e5: But notice: the pawn on c4 watches b5, and the pawn on a3 watches b4. The black king cannot go to those squares.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.livre.fala: Keep playing as White and see how Black defends.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.p: White to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.certo: Exactly! With your king on f5, the black king cannot keep the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to move the king away to f5. It looks strange, but this way the opposition becomes yours.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5d6.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5d6.2: The black king goes to b6. Only the pawn on c6 lies between the kings and White is to move: Black has the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5f6.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5f6.2: The black king goes to b6, on the same rank. There are three squares between the kings and White is to move: Black has the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5e6.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5e6.2: The black king goes to a6, on the same rank. There are three squares between the kings and White is to move: Black has the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5e4.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5e4.2: The black king climbs to a6. On the sixth and seventh ranks no square is watched by a pawn, and he always follows your king.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5f4.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5f4.2: The black king climbs to b6. On the sixth and seventh ranks no square is watched by a pawn, and he always follows your king.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.1: Now there are four squares between the kings, and Black is to move. To keep the opposition, the black king must leave an odd number.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.2: For that, he would have to go to b5, on the same rank. But the pawn on c4 watches that square.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.3: So the black king has to leave the fifth rank, and your king follows him on the new rank.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.4: The black king climbs to b6, to stay close to his pawns.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.5: You climb with him, to f6. Three squares between the kings: you have the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.6: The black king climbs one more rank, to b7.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.7: You climb again, to f7. Three squares between the kings: it is the distant opposition, and it is still yours.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.8: The black king returns to b6, next to his pawns.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.9: Careful now: the natural move would be to step down to e7. See what would happen.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.10: The white king steps down to e7.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.11: The black king goes to a7: three squares between the kings, and White is to move. It is the defence you just saw, and Black draws.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.12: White still wins, but with a king manoeuvre near the edge, which we will study later.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.13: Let's go back to the starting position. The key was the first move: the king on f5 left an even number of squares.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.14: The black king could not get back to an odd number, because the square he needed was watched by a pawn.
rot.edge.demos.aproximar.1: First position: the attack. Why not take the king straight to d6, next to the pawns?
rot.edge.demos.aproximar.2: The white king goes to d6 and attacks the pawn on c5.
rot.edge.demos.aproximar.3: The black king defends on b6. Only the pawn on c6 lies between the kings, and White is to move.
rot.edge.demos.aproximar.4: Black has the opposition. The white king must step back, and the white pawns cannot pass the turn.
rot.edge.demos.aproximar.5: That is why the white king moves away first: with him on f5, the watched square b5 decides the opposition.
rot.edge.demos.erroDefesa.1: Second position: now let's think from Black's side. What if the black king went to c7, next to the pawn on c6?
rot.edge.demos.erroDefesa.2: The black king goes to c7, facing the white king, with one square between them.
rot.edge.demos.erroDefesa.3: The white king goes to e6, on the way to d6, from where he would attack the pawn on c5.
rot.edge.demos.erroDefesa.4: To defend the pawn, the black king returns to b6.
rot.edge.demos.erroDefesa.5: The white king reaches d6. Only the pawn on c6 lies between the kings, and Black is to move: White has the opposition.
rot.edge.demos.erroDefesa.6: The black king has to leave b6, and the pawn on c5 is left undefended.
rot.edge.demos.erroDefesa.7: The white king captures the pawn on c5, and White wins.
rot.edge.demos.erroDefesa.8: On c7 the black king had the opposition, but he was far from b6. From a7, he returns to b6 with the opposition.
rot.edge.demos.erroDefesa.9: Your turn: one attack and one defence against the machine. Before each move, count the squares between the kings, pawns included.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Play White and find the best move. The pawns are blocked: only the kings move.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.fim: Your king moved away and used the square watched by the pawn to get the opposition.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.d5e6.1: 1.Ke6? brings your king closer to the pawns, but hands the opposition to Black: the win slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.d5e6.2: 1...Kg6! Only the pawn on f6 lies between the kings and White is to move: Black has the opposition.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.d5c6.1: 1.Kc6? takes your king to the sixth rank, but the black king follows: the win slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.d5c6.2: 1...Kg6! Three squares between the kings and White is to move: Black has the opposition.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.d5d6.1: 1.Kd6? takes your king to the sixth rank, but the black king follows: the win slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.d5d6.2: 1...Kh6! Three squares between the kings and White is to move: Black has the opposition.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.d5d4.1: 1.Kd4? steps back and lets the black king leave the fifth rank: the win slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.d5d4.2: 1...Kh6! On the sixth and seventh ranks no square is watched by a pawn, and the black king always follows yours.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.d5c4.1: 1.Kc4? steps back and lets the black king leave the fifth rank: the win slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.d5c4.2: 1...Kh6! On the sixth and seventh ranks no square is watched by a pawn, and the black king always follows yours.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.enunciado: Play Black and find the best move. The pawns are blocked: only the kings move.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.fim: Your king always answered on the same rank and kept the opposition.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.g6h6.1: 1...Kh6? goes to the sixth rank, but hands the opposition to White: the draw slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.g6h6.2: 2.Kd6! Three squares between the kings and Black is to move: White has the opposition.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.g6f7.1: 1...Kf7? faces the white king, but is far from g6: the draw slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.g6f7.2: 2.Kd6! If 2...Kg6, 3.Ke6!, with the pawn on f6 between the kings: White has the opposition.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.g6h5.1: 1...Kh5? moves your king away from the seventh rank: the draw slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.g6h5.2: 2.Ke7! If 2...Kg6, 3.Ke6!, with the pawn on f6 between the kings: White has the opposition.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.g6g7.1: 1...Kg7? leaves two squares between the kings, an even number: the draw slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.g6g7.2: 2.Ke7! Only f7 lies between the kings and Black is to move: White has the opposition.
